questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
questions.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\text{ }\text{ }2 & \text{ }1\,\,\,\,\,\, &  \\ -4 & \,\,-2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,1 & \text{ }0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}\text{ }\text{ }2 & \text{ }1\,\,\,\,\,\, &  \\ -4 & \,\,-2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,1 & \text{ }0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & \text{ }1\,\, &  \\ -4 & \text{ }-2\,\, \\ 1 & \,\,\,0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}10 \\ -5 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\text{ }\text{ }2 & \text{ }1\,\,\,\,\,\, &  \\ -4 & \,\,-2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,1 & \text{ }0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}21 & 10 \\ 10 & 5\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}44 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\text{ }\text{ }2 & \text{ }1\,\,\,\,\,\, &  \\ -4 & \,\,-2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,1 & \text{ }0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{5}[\begin{aligned}5 & \,-10 \\ -10 & \text{ }21\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}44 \\ 20\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\text{ }\text{ }2 & \text{ }1\,\,\,\,\,\, &  \\ -4 & \,\,-2\,\,\,\, \\ \,\,\,1 & \text{ }0\,\,\,\,\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -8 \\ 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ -8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}11 & -5 \\ -5 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{74}[\begin{aligned}9 & 5 \\ 5 & 11\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}6 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 3 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Subspace
questions.problem:
Verify whether the vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ are linearly independent, and find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}\,\,\,1 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}\,\,\,4 \\ -6 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we verify whether ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ are linearly independent. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ -1 & 3 & 1 \\ -1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, the pivot columns correspond to the linearly independent vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ that form the basis of our span.

Now, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the linearly independent columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}\,\,\,4 \\ -6 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ -6 & 14\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}14 & 6 \\ 6 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}12 \\ -26\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -5 \\ -4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Verify whether the vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ are linearly independent, and find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the vectors ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 1 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -2 \\ 10\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we verify whether ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}$ are linearly independent. So, we start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 2 & -4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & -4 \\ 0 & -3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, the pivot columns correspond to the linearly independent vectors ${a}_{1}$ and ${a}_{2}$ that form the basis of our span.

Now, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace spanned by the linearly independent columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ {a}_{1} & {a}_{2} \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-6 \\ -2 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 \\ 6 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}9 & -6 \\ -6 & 6\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Orthogonal Projection of a Vector Onto a Plane
questions.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane  $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ 5 & 9\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}9 & -5 \\ -5 & 3\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Notice that we obtained ${\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=x.$ This simply means that $x$ lies in the plane, i.e., 

$$
x\in \text{Span}{v,w}.
$$
